messages:
marina: FYI nightly evals flagged a big regression after the v22-int4 rollout. embedding-based reranks failing on legalqa-anchor-v2 promptset. cosine down across the board.

drew: ugh. numbers?

marina: quick stats from the nightly run:
- embedding cosine mean: baseline (v21-fp16) 0.87 -> v22-int4 0.62 (delta -0.25)
- top1 rerank accuracy: 0.78 -> 0.51
- a bunch of structured outputs now have malformed JSON (extra commas, truncated arrays)

chao: any tokenizer changes in v22? token offsets or merges updated?

marina: yes there was a small merge-table tweak to align with upstream tokenizer update. suspect mismatch between the model's vocab offsets and the tokenizer used in quantization pipeline.

elaine: can you paste a minimal repro generation that shows the JSON break?

marina: example from prompt id qa_2345:
```
System: extract citations in json
User: "Summarize and cite sources"
Model(v21): {"summary":"...","citations":[{"title":"...","url":"..."}]}
Model(v22-int4): {"summary":"...","citations":[{"title":"...","url":"...",},
```
trailing extra comma and newline insert before closing array.

drew: that smells like token-level insertion or tokenization boundary shifted. When quantized weights index embedding table differently you can get off-by-one token ids.

chao: I ran a quick diff on vocab offsets between the release build and the quant pipeline. Found that two tokens had their byte offsets shifted after running the merge update prior to quantization. pinging @ops-ian for the build artifacts.

ops-ian: CI-bot: build artifacts for redwood-v22-int4 available at s3://ci-artifacts/redwood/v22/int4/3141589000/

ci-bot: Canary deploy triggered for redwood-v22-int4 on canary pool: canary-west-1

marina: repro command to run locally:
```
python eval/nightly_run.py --model redwood-v22-int4 --promptset legalqa-anchor-v2 --shuffle-seed 42 --save-examples /tmp/v22-repro.jsonl
```

drew: I also ran an embedding-only test: compute embedding(v21) vs embedding(v22-int4) on 1k anchor queries, cosine histogram shows a clear left shift. Quick script:
```
# get embeddings
python scripts/get_embeddings.py --model v21 --promptset legalqa-anchor-v2 --out v21.npz
python scripts/get_embeddings.py --model v22-int4 --promptset legalqa-anchor-v2 --out v22.npz
python scripts/cosine_hist.py v21.npz v22.npz
```

chao: next actions I propose:
- pause canary (rollback to v21) until we confirm root cause :thumbsup:
- verify tokenizer merge table used at quantization time matches runtime tokenizer exactly
- re-run quantization with original merge table (or regenerate tokenizer artifacts from model repo)
- run targeted eval subset and compare per-token id diffs on failing prompts

elaine: +1. also add a quick unit test to nightly that asserts embedding cosine mean > 0.8 vs baseline for critical promptsets.

ops-ian: I paused the canary and rolled back traffic in canary-west-1. full rollback queued for 5m.

marina: Thanks. I'll run a token-id diff on the failing prompt and attach results here when done. If it's a tokenizer-vocab mismatch, we should treat it as a blocker for any further int4 rollouts.

drew: if it's not tokenizer, we should also check KV cache alignment in the int4 runtime path — off-by-one in position ids can cause JSON structure tokens to shift.

marina: quick dump from token-id diff for prompt qa_2345 (showing first 12 tokens):
v21 ids: [101, 2034, 9, 45, 102]
v22 ids: [101, 2034, 9, 46, 102]
note: a single token id substitution at index 3 (45 -> 46) which aligns with the merge-table change.

chao: that explains the comma insertion (token 46 is "," in this vocab). agreed blocker.

elaine: will add a CI check and create a follow-up to ensure quant pipeline consumes tokenizer artifacts from the same release tag. putting it on my plate.

marina: I opened a GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/modelops/issues/489 — description + repro + embeddings & token diffs attached.

drew: nice. assign to chao and elaine. any mitigation while we fix? maybe we can add a quick token remap layer in the runtime to accept old offsets for one release.

chao: possible but risky. prefer regenerate quant with the correct tokenizer. timeline: I can try regenerating overnight and run focused evals in the morning.

ops-ian: rollback complete across canary now. I'll monitor metrics and let us know if anything pops.

marina: thanks everyone. will post results of the regen run tomorrow AM. :coffee:
